sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: How will the Champions of AI programme sit alongside schemes like the Enterprise Innovation Scheme and the Productivity Solutions Grant, given that they are administered by different statutory boards under different Ministries?

sections.label: AI know-how for local IT firms
sections.summary: Asks whether MDDI can work with top AI firms and hyperscalers to transfer know-how to local IT firms, and whether GovTech can adopt these approaches and require government IT vendors to do the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Singapore's IT services firms are the delivery layer between our national AI strategy and real-world outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can MDDI work with the top AI firms and hyperscalers already based here to transfer such know-hows to our local firms?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) also move quickly to embrace these approaches, while adhering to cybersecurity and regulatory requirements, and progressively require IT service companies involved in Government work to do the same?

sections.label: Public Service Media headwinds
sections.summary: States that Public Service Media face significant headwinds: declining circulation, a fragmented media space, an evolving advertising model and growing overseas disinformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Yet, our Public Service Media face significant headwinds, declining circulation in a fragmented media space, a rapidly evolving advertising model and growing disinformation from overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: How does it do so to help them stay financially viable, so we can forestall similar painful restructuring here?

sections.label: Fake reports about Lee and Wong
sections.summary: Notes that many would have read fake online reports claiming Senior Minister Lee publicly disagreed with Prime Minister Wong.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Most recently, many of us would have read about the fake reports online claiming that Senior Minister Lee publicly disagreed with Prime Minister Wong.

sections.label: AI worsens information threat
sections.summary: States that AI worsens the threat because it can generate convincing content at scale, iterate rapidly and probe and undermine critical information infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: AI worsens the threat because it can generate convincing content at scale, iterate rapidly and be used to probe and undermine our critical information infrastructure.

sections.label: Singapore's global AI governance role
sections.summary: Recalls Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework of January 2019 and later work on Generative and Agentic AI, and asks what more the Government will do on global AI governance, standards, certification, coordination and capacity building.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Singapore has led with the Model AI Governance Framework of January 2019, a world first, and followed up with work on Generative and Agentic AI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Internationally, we could forge norms that prevent regulatory arbitrage and ensure cross‑border accountability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Hence, building on existing frameworks, what more will the Government do to strengthen Singapore's role in global AI governance, standards, certification, international coordination and capacity building, to preserve human agency while responsibly constraining AI agency?

sections.label: AI safety and anti-scam measures
sections.summary: Proposes a national AI safety curriculum, AI-specific online harms under the Online Safety Commission, and a public-private AI anti-scam taskforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: One, introduce a national AI safety curriculum across digital literacy programmes for different age groups and life stages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Two, the Online Safety Commission (OSC) can incorporate AI-specific risks into its categories of online harms by recognising AI-generated impersonations such as deepfakes and mass production of inauthentic materials to enable victims to seek timely remedies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Three, establish a public-private AI anti-scam taskforce to stay ahead of evolving threats and coordinate responses.

sections.label: Targeted rules for frontier AI
sections.summary: States frontier AI models pose a different category of risk, so Singapore should move toward targeted requirements for high-risk AI systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: And frontier AI models, the most powerful and unpredictable, pose a different category of risk altogether.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: That is why I believe Singapore should move toward targeted requirements for high‑risk or high‑impact AI systems rather than broad, one‑size‑fits‑all.

sections.label: Practical AI tools for SMEs
sections.summary: Says the refreshed National AI Strategy sets direction on trusted AI, but SMEs need practical tools like sector-specific trust roadmaps and governance templates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The refreshed National AI Strategy sets the direction on trusted AI, but SMEs need practical tools that they can use tomorrow – sector‑specific AI trust roadmaps that spell out common risks and good practices, pre-approved governance templates for data handling, model testing and human-in-the-loop check, simple "green‑lane" guidance so low‑risk use cases can move quickly while higher‑risk ones get the safeguards they need.

sections.label: SME governance and worker skills
sections.summary: Asks how SMEs can tap champions for governance support and how workers get role-specific skill maps and hands-on training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can MDDI share how SMEs can tap these champions for governance support, workflow redesign and to fully leverage national compute and enterprise schemes?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Workers need role‑specific skill maps to show how tasks will change with AI, clear pathways to move from today's roles to tomorrow's AI‑enabled, and hands‑on training tied to tools that SMEs are actually adopting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: When workers see how AI makes work easier and raises productivity, adoption becomes natural.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I welcome the Budget's investment in local AI developers and testbeds and the role of Government procurement in helping them scale.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: And as AI becomes more embedded in operations, the new Cyber Resilience Centre and enhanced SME support will give businesses the confidence to adopt AI safely.

sections.label: National AI Impact Programme
sections.summary: MDDI is creating the National AI Impact Programme, aiming to support 10,000 local enterprises over three years to integrate AI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: At stake are our entrepreneurs' hopes and dreams, workers' livelihoods and their communities' progress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is why MDDI is creating the National AI Impact Programme – to turn AI's possibilities into reality for the many, not the few.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Today, 15% of SMEs and about seven in 10 workers use AI in some way.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Over the next three years, the National AI Impact Programme aims to support 10,000 local enterprises to integrate AI into their business processes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: They make up 30% of the digital solutions on IMDA's SMEs Go Digital platform today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is why we are enhancing the Digital Leaders Programme and launching a new Digital Leaders Accelerator Bootcamp to build skills and confidence in change management and not just tech capabilities.

sentences.text: Second, we will provide CII owners with advanced tools, so that they are equipped to deal with advanced threats and.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)

sections.label: Helping CII owners against APTs

sentences.text: Oobee has scanned over 1,600 websites since 2023.

sections.label: Government scam protection steps
sections.summary: Mr Sharael Taha asked about efforts to protect citizens from scams, and steps taken include unifying Government SMS messages under the "gov.sg" sender ID.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Mr Sharael Taha asked about our efforts to protect citizens from scams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: We have already taken steps, for example, by unifying SMS messages from Government under the "gov.sg" sender ID.

sections.label: Postpaid SIM card limit
sections.summary: IMDA, in consultation with the Singapore Police Force, recently implemented a limit of 10 postpaid SIM cards per person across all telcos.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: To address this, IMDA, in consultation with the Singapore Police Force, recently implemented a limit of 10 postpaid SIM cards per person across all telcos.

sections.label: Institute of Digital Government
sections.summary: MDDI will establish the Institute of Digital Government together with the Civil Service College.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: MDDI will establish the Institute of Digital Government together with the Civil Service College.

sections.label: LifeSG parental services
sections.summary: Through LifeSG, parents can complete services like birth registration, apply for Baby Bonus and Shared Parental Leave, with far less paperwork.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Through LifeSG, parents can complete services like birth registration, apply for Baby Bonus and Shared Parental Leave, with far less paperwork.

sections.label: Nurse registration process streamlined
sections.summary: Registration processes are simplified and the Professional Registration System rebuilt, cutting foreign nurse registration from up to six months to 30 days.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Lengthy manual registration processes to bring in nurses can become a bottleneck that delays care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: And that is why we are simplifying our processes and rebuilding the Professional Registration System to streamline and automate routine checks for our healthcare professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: We have reduced processing time for foreign nurse registrations from up to six months to 30 days.

sections.label: Government policy and service delivery
sections.summary: Government officials are asked whether policies are delivered in the simplest way and whether they would accept the service experience for their own families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: All of us working in Government must ask ourselves: if we are responsible for a policy, is it being delivered in the simplest way possible?

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: If we are designing a service, ask: would I accept this experience for my own family?

sections.label: Singaporeans compare digital experiences
sections.summary: Singaporeans increasingly compare government digital services to the best digital experiences in their daily lives, not just to other governments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Increasingly, Singaporeans compare us to the best digital experiences in their daily lives, not just to governments elsewhere.

sections.label: Online Safety Commission established
sections.summary: The Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act establishes the Online Safety Commission by the first half of this year to support victims of five online harms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As part of the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act, we will establish a new agency, the Online Safety Commission (OSC).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The OSC will be set up by the first half of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: It will begin by supporting victims of five highly prevalent and severe online harms: online harassment; intimate image abuse; image-based child abuse; doxxing; and online stalking.

sections.label: App store age assurance measures
sections.summary: From the end of this month, designated app stores must implement age assurance measures to stop users under 18 accessing age-inappropriate apps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: From the end of this month, designated app stores will have to implement age assurance measures to prevent users who are under 18 from accessing and downloading age-inappropriate apps.

sections.label: Age assurance for social media
sections.summary: As MDDI studies the impact of social media bans, it plans to extend age assurance requirements to designated social media services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As MDDI continues to study the impact of social media bans, we plan to extend age assurance requirements to designated social media services.

sections.label: Smart Nation Educator Fellowship launch
sections.summary: MDDI and MOE launched the Smart Nation Educator Fellowship last year, with 58 fellows in the inaugural run.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Last year, MDDI and MOE launched the Smart Nation Educator Fellowship, and 58 fellows attended the inaugural run.

sections.label: Code for Fun AI update
sections.summary: IMDA and MOE are updating the Code for Fun programme to add AI skills, available to all schools in 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: IMDA is working with MOE to update the Code for Fun programme in our primary and secondary schools to integrate AI skills as core baseline capabilities for all students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We will make this available to all schools in 2027.

sections.label: DigitalAccess@Home for lower-income families
sections.summary: IMDA's DigitalAccess@Home scheme will continue supporting lower-income families with subsidised broadband and computing devices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For lower-income families, IMDA's DigitalAccess@Home scheme will continue to support them with subsidised broadband and computing devices.

sections.label: NLB SURE information literacy packages
sections.summary: NLB will roll out new resource packages and outreach programmes under SURE to build information literacy skills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: NLB will roll out new resource packages and outreach programmes under SURE to build information literacy skills.

sections.label: Langkah Digital for Malay/Muslim community
sections.summary: M3 launched Langkah Digital, led by Yayasan MENDAKI, built on three elements: Kenal, Guna and Yakin.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To work towards making our vision of an AI-Confident Malay/Muslim community a reality, M³ has launched Langkah Digital, led by Yayasan MENDAKI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As I announced last month, Langkah Digital is designed around three key elements – Kenal, Guna, Yakin.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Kenal (Knowing) helps people learn more about safe digital exploration; Guna (Use) encourages integrating technology in daily life; and Yakin (Confident) nurtures lifelong digital learning so that the community can continue to adapt independently.

sections.label: Langkah Digital workshops and participants
sections.summary: Since launching last month, 12 AI-related workshops and events have reached over 400 participants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Although I just launched the programme last month, I am heartened that we have rolled out 12 AI-related workshops and events in the community so far, reaching over 400 participants.

sections.label: Visitors to exhibition on Singapore path
sections.summary: Over 130,000 visited since December, with 96% saying they gained deeper understanding of Singapore's path.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Since December, over 130,000 have visited; 96% said they left with a deeper understanding of the path Singapore took.

sections.label: Freedom of Information Act proposal
sections.summary: Mr Fadli proposed a Freedom of Information Act to declassify records after 25 years, but it could lead to more opacity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Mr Fadli also raised the proposal for a Freedom of Information Act to automatically declassify records and release them publicly after 25 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In fact, implementing an Freedom of Information Act could lead unintentionally to more opacity.

sections.label: Transparency, governance and records access
sections.summary: A Freedom of Information Act can hinder governance, so transparency should prioritise good governance, and a public records access mechanism already exists.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In every system that goes down this path, what happens is that people watch what they put in writing and talk without committing to paper.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: It's a thoroughly bad way of analysing complex issues." In other words, a Freedom of Information Act can hinder rather than facilitate governance because issues deemed too sensitive are simply not documented.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Therefore, our starting point should be prioritising transparency that leads to good governance and an informed citizenry instead of transparency for its own sake.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We already have a mechanism for members of the public to request access to Government records for reference or research, which historians and researchers have used to nominate documents for review.

sections.label: SG60 Heart&Soul Experience visitors
sections.summary: The SG60 Heart&Soul Experience drew two million visitors in the second half of last year, letting Singaporeans express hopes and dreams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The SG60 Heart&Soul Experience, which was visited by two million visitors in the second half of last year, allowed Singaporeans to express their hopes and dreams for Singapore.

sections.label: NAIC authority and NAIS 2.0 progress
sections.summary: Questions ask whether NAIC will have execution authority or be advisory, how it integrates MTI and MDDI strategies, and what progress NAIS 2.0 has made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Will it have execution authority or oversee cross-Ministry implementation or remain advisory?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: And how will the NAIC integrate economic strategy under MTI with digital governance under MDDI to ensure a coordinated delivery?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Also, on NAIS 2.0, what progress has been made and what did we learn from implementing NAIS 2.0 that will shape our current plans?

sections.label: Trusted AI certification and NAIS 2.0
sections.summary: A formal trusted AI certification regime for high-risk systems is considered, and the Prime Minister launched NAIS 2.0 in December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Will we consider establishing a formal trusted AI certification regime for high-risk AI systems deployed in finance, healthcare and aviation?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Perhaps to address Mr Sharael Taha's question on what we have learned from the implementation of NAIS 2.0, the Prime Minister launched NAIS 2.0 in December 2023.

sections.label: Lorong AI growth and events
sections.summary: Lorong AI grew faster and bigger than expected, hosting about 150 events with 4,000 people last year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It turned out to move a lot faster and grow a lot bigger than we expected.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I think last year, Lorong AI hosted something like 150 events with about 4,000 people.

sections.label: Microsoft and Google DeepMind offices
sections.summary: Microsoft set up a research entity in Singapore last year, and Google DeepMind decided to open an office here.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Microsoft has been in Singapore for years, but it was only last year that they set up a research entity here.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Then Google DeepMind decided to open an office here.

sections.label: Prime Minister chairs National AI Council
sections.summary: The Prime Minister chairs the National AI Council, indicating Singapore's keenness to make AI transformation real for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Our Prime Minister has many things on his plate.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: He advises us on a whole range of things, but to chair the National AI Council is a very strong indication that we are keen on making AI transformation real for all Singaporeans and not just something that just continues to exist as a vision.

sections.label: AI safety and online safety institutions
sections.summary: Singapore set up a digital trust centre as its AI Safety Institute and a Centre of Advanced Technologies for Online Safety, and will seek industry and academia collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, quite apart from introducing model governance frameworks, we have set up a digital trust centre that is our designated AI Safety Institute.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We also have the Centre of Advanced Technologies for Online Safety.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These are institutions that have grown within academic organisations, but we will look for opportunities to collaborate with industry, with academia, to see how we can institutionalise this capability and turn it into an advantage for Singapore.

sections.label: Access to National AI Impact Programme
sections.summary: Citizens will access the National AI Impact Programme not solely through channels overseen by MDDI and IMDA.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in terms of how citizens are going to access the National AI Impact Programme, it again will not be solely through the channels that MDDI and IMDA oversee.

sections.label: Productivity Solutions Grant AI solutions
sections.summary: About 30% of Productivity Solutions Grant solutions are now AI-enabled.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Productivity Solutions Grant is well known to many of our enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I mentioned in my earlier speech that about 30% of the solutions are now AI-enabled.

sections.label: Accountancy and legal professions start
sections.summary: The speaker says work will start with the accountancy and legal professions, then extend to fields like human resources.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For individuals, I mentioned that we will start, initially, with the accountancy and legal professions and then look to extend towards fields like human resources (HR).

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: HR, for example, easily has 50,000 members, 50,000 practitioners.

sections.label: Elections online advertising legislation
sections.summary: The speaker says existing legislation is sometimes not enough, citing the Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising) legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But there will be instances where existing legislation, existing laws, existing measures are not enough.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, for example, we introduced the Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising), or ELIONA, legislation.

sections.label: AI translation for public websites
sections.summary: The National Translation Committee is working with GovTech and A*STAR on language models to translate public materials into Malay, Mandarin and Tamil.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The National Translation Committee has been working with GovTech and Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) on a number of LLMs and to fine tune a model for a local context.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: One of the objectives is to, hopefully, have a model which we can use by the later part of this year, to allow greater inclusivity and accessibility for those not speaking English to access our public-facing websites and other materials.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: And to support Public Service agencies translate many of the material, which is in English, into different mother tongue languages – Malay, Mandarin, Tamil – much more easily.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: And how can we do so across the board, at-scale, across the Public Service?

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: So, we are developing an AI tool for that and we hope to share more details in the later part of the year, but this is just one specific example how we are using AI technology.

sections.label: Optimising speed security cost trust
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore cannot optimise one dimension over another and must optimise across speed, security, cost and trust.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: And so, we cannot afford to optimise one dimension over another.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: It is very educational, and I hope more Singaporeans can understand that we must optimise across all dimensions – speed, security, cost and trust.

sections.label: Thanks to MDDI team
sections.summary: The speaker thanks ministers, the MDDI Permanent Secretary and team, and Members, then seeks leave to withdraw an amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I would like to take this opportunity to thank Minister Josephine Teo, Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How, Minister of State Rahayu, Minister of State Jasmin Lau and the Permanent Secretary of MDDI, and the whole MDDI team for the responses and the great work that they do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: I would also like to thank our GPC and fellow Members for submitting 25 cuts and with more than three hours of debate, leaving no stone unturned; and I am quite sure quite a few of us would like to ask a few more supplementary questions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Frontier models double in capacity within short cycles, agentic systems are emerging with autonomous decision-making capacity, and geopolitical contentions affect — The Chairman: Mr Sharael Taha.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: — MDDI must juggle many things at once, drive innovation, safeguard trust, develop the deep and broad-based skill sets, protect the vulnerable and secure national competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: That is no small task, and I would like to thank our team in MDDI for doing all of that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: And with that, Mr Chairman, I seek leave to withdraw my amendment.
